subject: BCP/DR: snapshot sampling methodology + compact restore checklist
body:
From: Jordan Avery <jordan.avery@mountainbank.com>

Cc: MountainBank Ops <ops@mountainbank.com>
Date: 2028-04-15T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: BCP request: sampling methodology for snapshots + restore checklist

Hi Rachel,

As part of our SIG/SOC2 review, we're validating how Redwood performs RTO sampling and small-file/metadata restores. Can you share a short methodology we can include in the questionnaire about:

- How snapshots are selected for sampling (criteria & frequency)
- Steps and timings for performing a small-files restore (metadata + blob verify)
- Expected RTO for a targeted sample (what you measure and reporting format)
- Any required witness steps or telemetry we need to collect during a live run

We don't need a full runbook — a concise methodology and a 1-page restore checklist would be ideal. If you have example artifacts (sample snapshot names, expected log excerpts, or a brief KV warmup procedure) please attach.

Can we get this by EOD Monday so we can incorporate into the SIG timeline?

Thanks,
Jordan
VP, Infrastructure Risk
Mountain Bank

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: BCP request: sampling methodology for snapshots + restore checklist

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached are two concise artifacts we use for customer audits: a one-page sampling methodology and a compact restore checklist. High-level answers inline below and in the attached PDF/worksheet.

Quick answers:
- Sampling criteria & cadence: we perform both scheduled and risk-triggered sampling. Scheduled: weekly rolling samples per region (1 full-volume snapshot + 3 small-file sets across customers). Risk-triggered: after infra changes or failed DR rehearsals.
- Small-files restore steps: snapshot mount -> metadata index verification -> selective object restore -> checksum validate -> post-restore smoke tests (API perf + DB integrity probes). Expectation: small-file set (up to 10k objects, typical ~50MB total) completes restore verification within 20–30 minutes in our standard dedicated pool; detailed timings are in the sheet.
- Measured RTO: we report time-to-serve (first successful API response for restored objects) and time-to-complete (all checks passed). Our sampling report shows median/95th percentiles; template included.
- Witnessing/telemetry: please capture the external timestamp, the snapshot id, and the test client request IDs. We will record server-side traces and provide a telemetry bundle (log excerpts, KV cache fill time) for your audit.

Next steps:
1) Review the attached artifacts (rto_sampling_methodology_v1.pdf, restore-checklist-compact.xlsx).
2) Confirm a 60-minute window for a live sample run this week if you want us to produce telemetry and a signed log bundle.

I'm looping in Marissa (CS lead) to coordinate scheduling and ops contacts.

-rk
Rachel Kim
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: rto_sampling_methodology_v1.pdf (attachment stub), restore-checklist-compact.xlsx (attachment stub)

Adding a few ops-technical notes (see attached kv-cache-warmup-playbook.md stub):

- Snapshot identifiers: we use region-code + date + seq (e.g., us-west2-20280412-snap-03). Include that id in your questionnaire response so reviewers can tie telemetry to an artifact.
- KV cache warmup: for samples that verify read latency we perform a targeted KV-prefill for the restored keyspace; typical warmup time observed is ~90–150s for a 10k-key set on a dedicated GPU pool. We capture the 'first-read' delta and the point at which token throughput stabilizes — both included in the sampling report.
- Small-file caveat: object-store tiering (cold vs warm) can add additional retrieval time. For audit samples we pin cold data to warm for the duration of the test.

Happy to run the live sample — I suggest we schedule for Wed 2028-04-18 14:00 PST. Ops, please confirm the maintenance window.

-ben
Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
